sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Guiera senegalensis is a shrub of dry savanna and fallow land in West Africa, usually 1–3 m tall and sometimes reaching 5 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The leaves are about 3–5.5 × 2–3 cm. Flowers are grouped in small spherical heads; the silky, spindle-shaped fruits are about 3–4.5 cm long.

sections.title: Reported uses
sections.text: Sources describe the leaves as famine food and roasted fruit powder in traditional cough remedies. These reported uses do not establish medical efficacy or safety.
